legal.summary: The Delhi High Court dismissed a petition challenging the framing of charges against a woman in a gang rape case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The court ruled that the term 'persons' in Section 376-D of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 70 of the POCSO Act is gender-neutral. This means that a woman can be charged if she acts in furtherance of a common intention to commit rape alongside others. The case underscores the court's interpretation that all individuals, regardless of gender, can be implicated in such serious offenses if they share a common intent.
